description: What was actually covered, per venue class. A class with no researcher coverage statement and no new research rows was carried entirely from the prior census and was NOT independently re-researched here.

source_families_checked: Wikipedia List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom (fully walked and diffed against ALREADY-COVERED.md INDOOR_ARENA list)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: Second-pass task, prompted by the coordinator flagging M&S Bank Arena Liverpool (11,000 cap, formerly Echo Arena) as completely absent from ALREADY-COVERED.md. Performed a full systematic diff of Wikipedia's List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom (19 constructed arenas) against the prior census's 39-venue INDOOR_ARENA list. Every other constructed arena traced to an already-covered venue under a current or historical sponsor name (Arena Birmingham=Utilita Arena Birmingham, Leeds Arena=first direct arena, Newcastle Arena=Vertu Motors Arena, Sheffield Arena=Canon Medical Arena, Cardiff International Arena=Utilita Arena Cardiff, Wembley Arena=OVO Arena Wembley, Manchester Arena=AO Arena, Commonwealth Arena/Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome=Emirates Arena, Swansea Arena=Swansea Building Society Arena) EXCEPT M&S Bank Arena, which is now added with a directly-fetched official-site identity confirmation and third-party-corroborated capacity. 'Proposed' (not-yet-built) and 'former/demolished' arenas on the Wikipedia list were correctly excluded as not being currently operating permanent venues. This is now the one venue_class in this researcher's output that can be called genuinely SYSTEMATIC rather than partial, because a comprehensive national list was walked in full and diffed, not sampled.

Checked known major UK permanent athletics stadia not already covered by the prior census under other classes. Several prominent athletics venues (Alexander Stadium, London Stadium, Gateshead International Stadium, Cardiff International Sports Stadium, Manchester Regional Arena, Queensway Stadium Wrexham, Crystal Palace National Sports Centre, Scotstoun Stadium) were checked and correctly skipped as already present under FOOTBALL_STADIUM/RUGBY_STADIUM/OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE. Of the genuinely new candidates: Antrim Forum confirmed at exactly 1,000; Mary Peters Track (Belfast, NI's national venue) and Woodside Stadium (Watford) confirmed below threshold; Grangemouth Stadium (Scotland's national athletics venue) and Bedford International Athletics Stadium (major England Athletics/National Athletics League venue) could not have a capacity figure evidenced despite repeated targeted searching and a direct fetch of the Grangemouth operator's own page, so both are emitted as CAPACITY_UNVERIFIED_HIGH_VALUE_CANDIDATE. Other National Athletics League-tier venues (Portsmouth Mountbatten Centre, Solihull Tudor Grange, Southampton, Yeovil, Exeter, Swansea, Stoke) were searched briefly, found to lack any strong 'obviously major' signal or capacity evidence, and were NOT added as rows to avoid diluting the census with minor leisure-centre tracks -- coverage of the full England Athletics regional-league venue tier is NOT systematic.

All 9 current Super League Basketball (men's, top tier) club venues were checked. 7 of 9 were already present in the prior census under INDOOR_ARENA. The remaining 2 (Bristol Flyers/SGS College Arena 750, Surrey 89ers/Surrey Sports Park 970) were newly evidenced but both fall below the 1,000 threshold and are emitted as BELOW_THRESHOLD rows for honesty. The lower-tier National Basketball League (NBL Division 1 and below, a feeder league of school/leisure-centre sports halls) was not systematically checked -- assumed sub-threshold and not chased given budget discipline, except University of Worcester Arena, which surfaced independently via the netball research and is emitted under MULTI_SPORT_ARENA.

source_families_checked: Wikipedia List of city and town halls in the United Kingdom (identified but NOT walked - see source-families.jsonl)
ad-hoc WebSearch for named regional town/city halls

researcher_coverage_statements.why: 8 rows across two passes (Margate Winter Gardens, Doncaster Dome, Corn Exchange Ipswich, Cheltenham Town Hall, St Andrew's Hall/The Halls Norwich, King's Lynn Corn Exchange - 6 CIVIC_HALL plus The Piece Hall Halifax as EVENT_HALL). Still no single national source-family (industry body, operator estate, or council-estate directory) covering UK civic halls was found in either pass; the England-alone Wikipedia list of town/city halls has 800+ entries and was deliberately NOT walked exhaustively (recorded as a conscious scope decision, not a negative finding) because each entry would need its own capacity lookup. Correctly excluded via verification rather than assumption: Wolverhampton Civic Hall/Southampton Guildhall/Preston Guild Hall/De Montfort Hall (all already covered under other names), Royal Hall Harrogate (950, official, below threshold), Manchester Town Hall (500, also currently closed for refurbishment since 2018), Cardiff City Hall (600), Plymouth Guildhall (840), Derby Assembly Rooms (CLOSED/disused since a 2014 fire, no confirmed reopening - correctly not treated as a current venue). This remains the weakest-covered priority class: a genuinely systematic national approach (e.g. walking GLL/Better's full venue estate, or every unitary/metropolitan council's own venues page) was never achieved.

The coordinator asked for a CONCERT_HALL diff-against-a-national-list only 'if budget remains' after arenas and theatres. A 'List of concert halls' Wikipedia page was identified (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_concert_halls, with a UK section) but was not fetched or diffed in this pass. This is an explicit, named remaining gap for a follow-up researcher, not a claim that CONCERT_HALL coverage is complete.

source_families_checked: stadium-hospitality-suite pattern search (Ashton Gate, St James' Park)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: 3 new rows in the second pass: East Midlands Conference Centre Nottingham (1,000, University of Nottingham's own conferencing brand, found via the Venues of Excellence sitemap), Lansdown Suite at Ashton Gate Stadium Bristol (1,000) and The Barracks at St James' Park Newcastle (1,000) - both distinct named conference/banqueting facilities at already-covered football stadiums. All three capacities sit exactly at the 1,000 threshold, sourced from the venue's own domain but not independently fetched, so capacity_confidence is MEDIUM throughout. The stadium-hospitality-suite pattern (see EXHIBITION_CENTRE note) was only checked for 2 of England's ~92 professional football grounds plus 1 racecourse - a systematic pass across the full FOOTBALL_STADIUM/RUGBY/RACECOURSE lists in ALREADY-COVERED.md for equivalently large named conference suites was not attempted and is a real remaining gap.

International Convention Centre Wales (ICC Wales, Newport) was surfaced as a candidate but turned out to already be in ALREADY-COVERED.md (under MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX, not CONVENTION_CENTRE - a possible cross-class naming note for the coordinator). No genuinely new CONVENTION_CENTRE row was found or emitted in either pass.

source_families_checked: ad-hoc WebSearch (incidental to civic-hall and arena research)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: 2 rows found (The Piece Hall Halifax, 5,500 outdoor courtyard; The Auditorium Liverpool, 1,350 seated, found as a byproduct of confirming M&S Bank Arena's capacity) but neither pass performed a deliberate, systematic search specifically for this class.

source_families_checked: Wikipedia Category:Exhibition and conference centres in England

researcher_coverage_statements.why: 3 rows across two passes: The NEC/National Exhibition Centre (10,000+, official source - a major national-scale miss now fixed), Centenary Pavilion at Elland Road Leeds (2,800, distinct facility at an already-covered stadium site), and Doncaster Racecourse Exhibition Centre (3,000, distinct facility at an already-covered racecourse site). This third pattern - a large, separately-named, separately-bookable exhibition/conference facility co-located with an already-covered sports venue - proved to be a real and repeatable source of gaps (also found for CONFERENCE_CENTRE, see Lansdown Suite/Ashton Gate and The Barracks/St James' Park) and is worth the coordinator systematically checking across ALL already-covered football/rugby/cricket grounds and racecourses, not just the handful spot-checked here. Did not systematically walk ASM Global's full UK estate or GL events UK.

source_families_checked: National Ice Hockey League clubs (individual club/venue sites)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: All 10 current EIHL (top tier) club arenas were checked and found to already be present in the prior census's committed 855-venue list under INDOOR_ARENA -- zero new EIHL rows were needed; this is the headline finding for this class. Below EIHL, the National Ice Hockey League (NIHL, 2nd/3rd tier, roughly 30 rinks nationwide across National/Division 1 North/Division 1 South) was only partially checked: 3 rinks (Telford Ice Rink, Link Centre Swindon, Planet Ice Peterborough) were individually verified via genuine sources as clearing 1,000 and are emitted as rows. Roughly 15-20 further NIHL rinks (Basingstoke, Bristol, Hull, Leeds, Milton Keynes, Solway Sharks, Billingham, Blackburn, Deeside, Nottingham, Sheffield Scimitars, Solihull, Cardiff Fire, Chelmsford, Romford x2, Slough, Solent, Streatham, Widnes) were NOT individually verified this package. A WebFetch summary of Wikipedia's NIHL page produced implausible uniform capacity claims (every rink >=1000, self-contradicting) that were explicitly rejected as unreliable rather than used as evidence -- see source-families.jsonl. A genuine venue-by-venue NIHL sweep was not completed within budget; one-search-per-small-rink was judged poor value against the source-family-first mandate, since most are small leisure-centre rinks plausibly below 1,000.

source_families_checked: ad-hoc WebSearch per city (London, Birmingham, Manchester, Glasgow, Cardiff, Leeds, Edinburgh, Belfast, Liverpool, Newcastle, Bristol)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: Prior census had ZERO venues in this class; across both passes this researcher adds 10 rows, all CONFIRMED_1000_PLUS but only 2 sourced from a page this researcher actually fetched directly (desouza-associates.com); the rest rest on WebSearch snippets of the hotel's own domain - capacity_confidence is MEDIUM (or LOW for Sheraton Grand Edinburgh, whose 1,000 figure is an explicit combined-two-room claim) throughout, and several sit exactly at or just above the 1,000 threshold. Second pass specifically targeted the cities the first pass had NOT covered (Liverpool, Newcastle, Bristol, Edinburgh) as instructed: Liverpool and Newcastle/Bristol hotel ballrooms all came back BELOW 1,000 (Titanic Hotel Liverpool 994; Bristol Hotel ballroom 400) so no new hotel rows exist for those three cities - only stadium-based conference suites (a different venue_class) were found there instead. Edinburgh yielded one hotel row (Sheraton Grand, weakly evidenced). Belfast hotels were checked and found below/ambiguous at the threshold (Crowne Plaza Belfast: conflicting 900 vs 1,000 claims, not resolved, no row emitted). No hotel operator group (all IHG, all Hilton, all Marriott UK properties) was walked as a full estate in either pass.

Checked venues used by Netball Super League clubs that were not already shared with an already-covered arena: Team Bath Arena, Cardiff City House of Sport, Essex Sport Arena, University of Worcester Arena (all confirmed >=1000) and English Institute of Sport Sheffield (major multi-sport venue, capacity unverified). Other NSL/NSLW-associated venues (Sheffield Hatters, Nottingham Wildcats, Oaklands Wolves secondary venues, and NSL showcase fixtures hosted one-off at already-covered arenas such as The O2 and OVO Arena Wembley) were not individually chased. M&S Bank Arena Liverpool was discovered as a significant general-arena gap (~11,000 capacity, used for Manchester Thunder and Cardiff Dragons netball fixtures, not present anywhere in the census under any name) but was logged to handoff.jsonl rather than researched further, since it is fundamentally a general concert/exhibition arena (comparable to AO Arena/OVO Hydro, both already covered) outside this researcher's assigned sport-specific scope.

Speedway was worked league-by-league and systematically. All 6 current SGB Premiership (top tier) tracks were checked: Belle Vue/National Speedway Stadium confirmed 6,500; Ipswich/Foxhall confirmed ~10,000; King's Lynn/Adrian Flux Arena, Leicester/Beaumont Park, Northampton Shaleway all identity-confirmed as permanent professional venues but capacity unverified; Sheffield/Owlerton found already covered by the prior census under greyhound racing; Perry Barr Stadium (Birmingham Brummies) checked and found to have CLOSED in 2025, correctly excluded rather than emitted as an active venue. Of the 9 SGB Championship (tier 2) tracks, the 4 highest-profile were checked (Edinburgh/Armadale Stadium, Glasgow/Saracen Park, Poole/Wimborne Road Stadium confirmed >=1000 via a partial grandstand figure, Redcar/South Tees Motorsports Park) -- the remaining ~5 Championship tracks (Scunthorpe, Isle of Wight, Plymouth, Berwick, and any others) were NOT individually checked. Velodromes, major tennis and swimming/aquatics venues were checked and found to be either already covered (National Cycling Centre Manchester, Lee Valley VeloPark, Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome, Derby Arena, All England Club, Queen's Club, London Aquatics Centre, Sandwell Aquatics, Ponds Forge, Nottingham Tennis Centre) or below threshold (Geraint Thomas National Velodrome of Wales, 500). Darts/snooker/boxing regular-host venues were not separately researched since the well-known ones are either already covered (Utilita Arena Sheffield) or general arenas outside scope (M&S Bank Arena, logged to handoff).

source_families_checked: List of British rugby league stadiums by capacity (Wikipedia, used only as a discovery/cross-check lead)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: Cross-checked every current Super League and RFL Championship club ground against the already-covered list using a third-party capacity table as a discovery lead. The large majority (Odsal, MKM Stadium Hull, Brick Community Stadium, Headingley, BrewDog Stadium, Halliwell Jones, Boundary Park, DCBL Stadium Widnes, Craven Park Hull, Morson Stadium Salford, Leigh Sports Village, The OneBore Stadium Castleford, The Shay, Kingston Park, Derwent Park, Spotland, Post Office Road, DIY Kitchens Stadium Wakefield, Plough Lane/London Broncos, York Community Stadium, Craven Park Barrow, Cougar Park, Mount Pleasant, Recreation Ground Whitehaven, Stadiwm Eirias, Crown Flatt, South Leeds Stadium, Club Doncaster Sports Village/Eco-Power Stadium, Steel City Stadium/Sheffield Eagles) were confirmed already present in the prior census's FOOTBALL_STADIUM or RUGBY_STADIUM lists, usually because the ground is shared with a football or rugby union tenant under a different current sponsor name. Two genuine gaps were found and evidenced: Heywood Road, Sale (Swinton Lions, confirmed 3,387) and Fartown Ground, Huddersfield (amateur Pennine League use, capacity deliberately left unverified rather than asserting a stale historic figure). Women's Super League grounds (e.g. Edge Hall Road, Wigan) were not individually checked.

source_families_checked: Wikipedia List of theatres in the United Kingdom (fetched and diffed against ALREADY-COVERED.md's 97-venue THEATRE list)

researcher_coverage_statements.why: Second-pass, lower-priority task done after the arena sweep, per the coordinator's instruction to attempt a diff-against-a-national-list technique for THEATRE/CONCERT_HALL if budget allowed. Fetched Wikipedia's UK theatre list and diffed every venue with a stated capacity of roughly 1,000+ against ALREADY-COVERED.md. Two apparent gaps (Birmingham Repertory Theatre, Leeds Playhouse) were independently verified against each venue's own official site and found to be BELOW the 1,000 threshold (816 and 850 respectively) - the Wikipedia page's capacity figures for these two entries were wrong (likely a WebFetch table-extraction error, the same failure mode caught on the indoor-arenas list for 'Vaillant Live'). No genuine THEATRE gap was found. Recorded as SYSTEMATIC because the comparison was exhaustive against the named list, not because every UK theatre was checked - a different national list (e.g. a paid industry directory) might still surface something this one did not.

source_families_checked: Academic Venue Solutions (partial - blocked by pagination tooling limitation)
VisitScotland Business Events academic venue page

researcher_coverage_statements.why: Prior census had ZERO venues in this class; across both passes this researcher adds 7 CONFIRMED_1000_PLUS rows (Great Hall Birmingham, Sport Central Northumbria, Sir David Wallace Sports Hall Loughborough, Sports Training Village Bath, Y Plas Cardiff, Central Campus Venues Warwick Conferences, plus Surrey Sports Park flagged REVIEW_REQUIRED for conflicting capacity figures never resolved). The Academic Venue Solutions directory (~70 members, exactly the source family this class most needed) was confirmed BLOCKED by a genuine tooling limitation in the second pass: repeated attempts at different pagination URL patterns (?paged=2, ?paged=3, /page/2/) all returned the identical first 10 members, indicating JS/AJAX-driven pagination that this WebFetch tool cannot traverse - roughly 60 of ~70 AVS members were never seen. This is the single biggest concrete blocker identified in this researcher's work and should be handed to a tool capable of executing JavaScript (e.g. a headless-browser-capable fetch) rather than retried with WebFetch. Below-threshold venues checked and excluded: Younger Hall St Andrews (958, official), Whitworth Hall Manchester (550-600, official), Queen Mary Great Hall (770), Conference Aston Great Hall (600), Keele Hall (~600), NTU (ambiguous, not resolved either way).
